# Contributor-triggerable re-review: a `recheck-review` comment re-runs any LLM-Review that is not a real finding

## Problem

An `LLM-Review -1` has two different meanings and only one contributor response: a **real
finding** (`[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]`) is fixed by amending; every OTHER `-1` — the
coverage-gap family (`gate-disabled`, `llm-unavailable`, `scanner`, `review-error`,
`indeterminate`, `merge-review`), including a retry-budget escalation from ticket
0347-b2cc-e6e9-4f6b — is an infrastructure veto the contributor can do nothing about.
Today the only remedies are an operator-run `/rerun` (SSM-token-gated; see
`infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`) or amending to spin a new patchset. CI already gives
contributors `recheck` for a `Verified -1` flake; the LLM lane has no equivalent. This
mirrors the OSS norm (Zuul/OpenStack `recheck`, Prow `/retest`) with one deliberate
restriction: LLM reviewers are stochastic, so retrying a REAL finding would be dice-rolled
self-approval — the retry surface must exclude findings.

## Approach

**Trigger surface: a Gerrit comment containing `recheck-review`** (its own token —
`recheck` stays CI's). Wire it end to end:

1. **Event plumbing** — `infra/gerrit/webhooks.config` gains `event = comment-added`
   alongside `patchset-created` (the plugin sends only listed types). Note in the file +
   ticket comment: an operator must re-run `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` to push the
   rendered config to `refs/meta/config` before the trigger goes live; until then the
   code path is inert (no events arrive).
2. **Routing** — the receiver's `/webhook` already enqueues every payload; the worker
   (`app.py::_worker`) routes `type == "comment-added"` to a NEW module
   `src/rebar/review_bot/retrigger.py` (voter.py is at ~670/800 LOC post-0347; this is a
   separate concern and its own seam) instead of `review_and_vote`. All other types keep
   the existing path.
3. **`retrigger.handle_comment_added(event, config, gerrit, dedup)`** does, in order:
   - **Loop guard**: ignore comments authored by the bot itself (`cfg.bot_user`), else the
     bot's own replies re-trigger events forever.
   - **Token match**: the comment text must contain `recheck-review` (word match, not
     substring of another word); anything else is a silent skip.
   - **Eligibility — decided privileged-side from durable Gerrit state, never from the
     requesting comment**: fetch the bot's change messages via
     `GET /a/changes/{id}/messages` (ChangeMessageInfo), select the latest entry whose
     `_revision_number` equals the current patchset AND whose author is the bot account,
     strip Gerrit's prepended `Patch Set N:` header block (the tag line is the first
     non-empty line AFTER that header — verify the exact preamble shape against a live
     capture during implementation and pin it in a fixture), then parse the tag line.
     The tag grammar is WIDER than `_TAG_SUFFIXES` and the parser must cover all three
     production sites, test-asserted per case: (a) the `_TAG_SUFFIXES` vocabulary
     (adapter.py:44), (b) the hardcoded `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap
     (merge-review)]` literal emitted by `voter.py::_merge_coverage_gap_decision`
     (voter.py:222) which is NOT a `_TAG_SUFFIXES` member, and (c) the merge-change
     variant that appends ` (merge-change, N integrated commit(s))` INSIDE the tag
     brackets (adapter.py:81-83) to any of the above. Parse by STEM: strip a trailing
     `(merge-change, …)` suffix first, then classify the remainder. The ONLY ineligible
     state is a current-revision finding-BLOCK — a tag whose stem is
     `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]`, INCLUDING its merge form
     `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, N integrated commit(s))]` (a dedicated
     test asserts the merge-form finding is refused): a real finding is refused — fix and
     re-push. Everything else is eligible: every coverage-gap sub-reason (including
     `merge-review` and a 0347 retries-exhausted escalation), a PASS (a fresh review can
     only produce a fresh verdict — it can flip PASS to BLOCK, which is
     fail-closed-safe, and never mints an unearned PASS), a vote-less change (harmless:
     equivalent to a reconciler re-drive), and an UNPARSEABLE or absent tag (fail-open
     to a fresh fail-closed review — re-reviewing is always safe; refusing must be
     reserved for the one proven-finding state).
   - **On refusal**: post a short reply comment (a message, never a vote) telling the
     contributor the `-1` is a real finding and the path is amend + re-push; emit a
     greppable `RETRIGGER_REFUSED` log marker.
   - **On acceptance**: `dedup.reset_attempts(change_id, current_revision)` (the 0347
     budget DELETE — the shared-budget harmonization: the human trigger re-arms the
     bounded automatic retries), enqueue the change's current revision with the existing
     `_rebar_force` marker (the `/rerun` force path — bypasses dedup + existing-vote
     short-circuits, still fail-closed), post a short "re-review queued" reply, and emit
     `RETRIGGER_ACCEPTED`.
4. **Harmonize `/rerun`** — the operator endpoint also resets the attempts budget before
   enqueueing (today it would force a review that could immediately re-escalate on a
   stale budget). `/rerun` keeps its unrestricted semantics (an operator may force even a
   finding re-review); the finding-refusal applies only to the contributor comment path.
5. **Gerrit client** — add the two small REST calls `retrigger` needs if absent:
   `get_change_messages(change_id)` (`GET /a/changes/{id}/messages`), and
   `post_comment(change_id, revision, message)` = `POST
   /a/changes/{id}/revisions/{rev}/review` with a JSON body containing ONLY `message` —
   **no `labels` key at all**. Never use a `labels: {LLM-Review: 0}` form: value 0 is
   still a label write and can displace/copy label state. A unit test asserts the
   serialized request body for the reply path has no `labels` member.

### Security property (must be tested, not just implemented)

A `recheck-review` comment on a change whose current revision carries a findings-BLOCK
does NOT enqueue a review, does NOT reset the budget, and does NOT touch the vote —
asserted by a dedicated test. Also asserted: the bot's own comments never trigger, and a
non-matching comment is a no-op. The trigger can only ever request a FRESH review through
the same fail-closed pipeline; nothing in this path writes a vote directly.

## Scope

- `infra/gerrit/webhooks.config` — `event = comment-added`.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/retrigger.py` (new) — routing target, eligibility, replies.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py` — worker routes `comment-added` to `retrigger`; `/rerun`
  gains the budget reset.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py` — message-fetch / comment-post helpers if absent.
- `docs/review-policy.md` — the coverage-gap rows' "Your productive response" becomes
  "comment `recheck-review`"; document the finding refusal.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` §2c — mention `recheck-review` beside `recheck`.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — note the contributor path; `/rerun` stays the
  operator escape hatch.
- Tests in `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` (worker routing) and a new
  `tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: a `recheck-review` comment on a change whose current-revision tag is any
      coverage-gap sub-reason resets the attempts budget, enqueues a forced re-review,
      and posts the "queued" reply — asserted by tests (at least gate-disabled and a
      retries-exhausted escalation case).
- [ ] AC2 (security property): the same comment on a findings-BLOCK revision — BOTH the
      bare `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]` tag AND the merge form
      `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, N integrated commit(s))]` — is
      refused: no enqueue, no budget reset, no vote change, refusal reply posted,
      `RETRIGGER_REFUSED` emitted — asserted by dedicated tests for both tag forms.
- [ ] AC2b: the tag parser classifies all three production tag shapes — `_TAG_SUFFIXES`
      members, the hardcoded `merge-review` literal (voter.py:222), and any tag carrying
      the in-tag `(merge-change, …)` suffix — and an unparseable/absent tag is treated
      as ELIGIBLE (fail-open to a fresh fail-closed review) — asserted by a parametrized
      test.
- [ ] AC2c: the refusal/queued reply path posts a message with NO `labels` key in the
      Gerrit REST body (never a value-0 label write) — asserted by a test on the
      serialized request.
- [ ] AC3: comments by the bot itself and comments without the token are no-ops (no
      reply, no enqueue) — asserted by tests.
- [ ] AC4: `/rerun` resets the attempts budget before enqueueing — asserted by a test.
- [ ] AC5: `webhooks.config` lists `comment-added`; the file's comment and the runbook
      state that `service-user.sh` must be re-run to activate it.
- [ ] AC6: `docs/review-policy.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` §2c document `recheck-review`
      (incl. the finding refusal).
- [ ] AC7: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the review-bot test modules pass; every
      touched/new `src/rebar` module stays within the 800-LOC cap (new module ≥100 LOC).

## Testing / Verification

From the worktree venv:
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint && env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`

## Relationship to 0347

Lands AFTER 0347-b2cc-e6e9-4f6b (this ticket consumes its `review_attempts` ledger and
`reset_attempts` DELETE semantics). 0347 handles the automatic recovery (vote-less defer +
bounded escalation); this ticket is the human escape hatch that re-arms it once the
underlying failure is corrected.
